name: Maudslay screw-cutting lathe
summary: Maudslay's lathe used change gears and a leadscrew to cut accurate screw threads, a key tool for precise, repeatable engineering work.
description: Hand-driven lathe with change-geared spindle and leadscrew, slide rest and micrometer feed, Science Museum object 1900-20.
tier_reason: Prefer promotion for the screw-cutting architecture and its machine-tool role; the circa1800 object date beats a by1831 death-bound for the same item. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: by 1831
date.basis: The museum says Maudslay used the surviving lathe; he died in 1831, so his own use must predate that year.

events.statement: The surviving lathe was used by Maudslay to make accurate screw threads; the museum dates the machine to around 1800.
events.caveats: Exact individual shop orders, first use and original change gears are not documented by this source; the death-year bound is inferential.

evidence.supports: Identifies the machine, screw manufacturing use and construction.
